text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGERS: multiple SRV lookup failures reported in us-central1 (us-central1c <-> us-central1d fabric). Paging jamie_oncall and lina_sre. Console: https://console/redwood/incident/2795550000

jamie_oncall: Acknowledged. Looking at CoreDNS and Consul dashboards. Any recent infra changes in us-central1?

lina_sre: CoreDNS upstream error rate spiked at 15:12:05Z. Consul shows repeated raft proposals timeouts and leader re-election around same window. et*cd* looks healthy but inter-AZ packet loss is high.

omar_netops: We saw BFD session flaps between aggregation switches in AZ c/d starting ~15:11Z. BFD withdrawal caused transient path churn and asymmetric routing. Opening provider case now.

sophia_infra: Sample pod resolver logs:```
15:11:58 resolver: SRV lookup _http._tcp.payments.svc.cluster.local failed: deadline exceeded (500ms)
15:12:03 coredns[proxy]: read udp 10.10.3.4:50321->10.200.12.9:53: i/o timeout
15:12:07 consul: rpc error: dial tcp 10.11.9.5:8300: connection refused
```

jamie_oncall: Initial mitigation plan: 1) quarantine flaky fabric route to avoid oscillation, 2) scale CoreDNS and switch node-local resolvers to prefer cache, 3) enable Consul maintenance on candidate servers to stop raft churn. Executing step 1 now.

omar_netops: Applying route-blackhole on nodes that prefer the bad next-hop in us-central1c:```
sudo ip route add blackhole 10.200.12.0/24
# verify
ip route get 8.8.8.8
```

lina_sre: After blackholing bad path, Consul RPC p99 latency down from ~2.3s to ~140ms. CoreDNS upstream timeouts decreased by ~72%. Some services still hit stale SRV data for endpoints that were routed over the now-blackholed path — TTL is 60s for these SRV records.

sophia_infra: Scaling CoreDNS from 2->6 replicas in us-central1 cluster and flipping node-local stub to prefer local cache. Deployed.

incident-bot: Update logged: mitigations applied. Incident ID INC-279555. Severity auto-eval: P1 if customer-facing >8%. Currently borderline.

tom_support: Two customer tickets flagged elevated 502s on ingest endpoints (tickets 55890, 55892). Both customers report errors concentrated on us-central region.

jamie_oncall: Apply mesh fallback: services will prefer consul agent-local SRV answers and fall back to configured static A records if lookup fails twice. Pushing config flag: mesh.srv_fallback=enabled

lina_sre: Also temporarily increasing sidecar retry backoff to reduce retry storm: backoff base 200ms -> 800ms; max retries 3 -> 2.

omar_netops: Provider case submitted: PROV-11988 (BFD session instability on inter-AZ fabric). Attached pcap, BGP logs, and sample traceroute. Asking for expedited investigation.

sophia_infra: To stabilize Consul leader, I'm putting the three most-stable servers into maintenance mode so they don't trigger elections:```
consul maint -server -id=server-7 -ttl=30m -reason="stabilize raft after fabric event"
consul maint -server -id=server-8 -ttl=30m -reason="stabilize raft after fabric event"
consul maint -server -id=server-9 -ttl=30m -reason="stabilize raft after fabric event"
```

jamie_oncall: Metrics: affected RPC error rate peaked at 12.7% and has fallen to 1.2% over the last 5m. Customer impact appears resolved.

tom_support: Customers 55890/55892 report improved success rates after ~3 minutes. I've posted interim status in their tickets.

lina_sre: Creating short-term remediation tasks: 1) add BFD health gating to route changes, 2) reduce SRV TTL for control-plane endpoints in us-central1 from 60s -> 15s, 3) document consul maintenance runbook.

jamie_oncall: Opening follow-ups: INF-4730 (BFD gating), INF-4731 (SRV TTL policy), INF-4732 (consul-maint runbook).

incident-bot: Follow-up tickets INF-4730, INF-4731, INF-4732 created. Incident state -> MONITORED.

victor_pm: Draft status page message: "We've observed transient service discovery failures in us-central1 caused by inter-AZ fabric instability. Services have been routed around the affected path and DNS/consul mitigations applied. We continue to monitor and will publish a postmortem."

tom_support: Customers acknowledged the update and requested ETA for RCA — I've promised initial findings within 48h.

jamie_oncall: Handoff: I need to step off in 35 minutes. Lina, can you monitor for 2 hours? I'll dump logs and commands into the incident doc before leaving.

lina_sre: Acknowledged. I'll take the monitoring window and begin RCA skeleton. Leaving note to confirm provider fix before removing blackhole and consul maintenance.

sophia_infra: One extra note — we'll add an alert rule to detect SRV TTL churn >2x baseline so we catch heavy cache invalidation storms quickly.

jamie_oncall: Closing pager (mitigated). Will run through timeline and start the postmortem with Lina. :white_check_mark:
